$comment: §GA-GATE-RATCHET (L-775) — DECLARED DEBT. SHRINK-ONLY.
These gates fail TODAY. They are drift that accumulated while the runner was
broken (L-774: spawnSync could not execute npx on win32, so all 25 reported
FAILED with no output and the suite was never wired into CI).
RULES:
1. A gate NOT on this list that fails is a REGRESSION and blocks CI.
2. A gate ON this list that starts PASSING is also a failure — remove its
line in the same commit that fixes it. Paid debt must leave the ledger,
or this file rots into a list of things that are secretly fine.
3. NOTHING may be ADDED here without an explicit founder/architect decision.
Adding a line is choosing to ship a known contract violation.
Baselined 2026-08-08 from the first successful run of the suite:
9 passing / 16 failing. Every removal below is real progress toward C01 §5,
which states all gates MUST pass before a PR merges — currently untrue.

2026-08-11 · §FIX-ISOLATION-GATE-BLIND (L-827) — REMOVED check-project-isolation.ts.
Third occurrence of the L-811 shape, and the worst of them. The gate reported 0
hits for ALL FOUR C13 anchors, on every Windows run, while all four were PRESENT
in source (measured 33 / 3 / 1 / 1). It shelled out via
execSync('grep -c "pat" "file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0'). execSync on win32 runs
under cmd.exe, where 2>/dev/null is a redirect to a nonexistent path: the command
fails, '|| echo 0' fires, and the gate reads a literal 0.
It did NOT throw. That is what made this worse than L-811. An ENOENT crash is
honest; this returned a well-formed number that LOOKED like a measurement, so
'I could not run' and 'I looked and found nothing' were the same value.
And it sat on THIS LEDGER, which is how it survived. A ledgered gate hides its
own blindness: the one state nobody investigates is the one they already expect.
The ledger asserted 'C13 isolation is known-broken' when the truth was 'C13
isolation is intact and unmeasured'. Rule 2 exists for exactly this — and note
that rule 2 alone would NOT have caught it, because the gate never started
passing; it never ran at all.
Rewritten Node-native (node:fs only, no shell) it PASSES all four anchors. Two
further hardenings, neither of which loosened a threshold — the minHits are the
originals, they simply evaluate for the first time:
• A missing subject file now exits 2 (MISCONFIGURED), never 0 and never 1.
Exit 1 is absorbable via this ledger; exit 2 never is. Conflating 'cannot
read the subject' with 'the anchor is gone' is the bug itself.
• Counts are taken AFTER stripComments(). This mattered immediately:
BatchCoordinator.ts has 33 raw mentions of forceReset and only 2 in code.
Counting raw text would let documentation satisfy the gate — the
§RAF-GATE-COMMENT-BLIND lesson (2026-08-10), second occurrence.
The decision logic is extracted to lib/projectIsolationAnchors.ts and negative-
tested in __tests__/projectIsolationAnchors.spec.ts (8 tests). T3 pins NO_SUBJECT
=> exit 2 and is the only test that would have caught the original defect.

2026-08-11 · §FIX-ZONING-GATE-MISSLICE (W1-4) — REMOVED
check-zoning-fidelity-label.ts. This one inverts the audit's finding, and the
inversion is the lesson. The audit recorded it as 'GISAreaLayout.ts:2770 — 2 of 6
refusal arms omit r.code'. THE RENDER WAS ALREADY HONEST: all four real refusal
arms interpolate ${escHtml(r.code)}. The GATE was falsely accusing the source.
It sliced its region from `const reasonLine =` to a LATER `panel.innerHTML =`
statement and harvested 'arms' with a naive /`[^`]*`/g, so it swept in a
backtick-quoted path inside a COMMENT and the manualZoneAffordance ADMIN BUTTON
template. Neither can carry a refusal code. 'Fixing' the render as instructed
would have meant stamping a refusal code onto a button — damaging an honest
render to satisfy a bad regex. GISAreaLayout.ts was NOT modified.
Worse than a false positive: while this gate sat here accusing a phantom, a REAL
codeless arm added next door would have been invisible inside the same count.
A blind gate and a lying gate fail the same way — they both make the number mean
something other than what it says.
Rewritten with a template-literal-aware tokenizer (comment and string bodies
blanked before slicing), content-based subject discovery via scanFiles() so a
RENAME cannot blind it, and four honesty floors (MIN_SCANNED_FILES,
MIN_SUBJECT_FILES, MIN_REFUSAL_ARMS, MIN_CONFIDENCE_TIERS) that exit 2. Setup
failures that used to exit 1 now exit 2, so this ledger can no longer absorb a
blind zoning gate. Nothing was relaxed: every arm must still carry r.code, and
the negative test proves a stripped code still FAILS — now counted correctly as
1 of 4 rather than the phantom 2 of 6. 19 specs in
__tests__/zoningFidelityLabelScan.spec.ts; the gate previously had no test.
NOTE: the agent also enumerated ~15 OTHER codeless-refusal render sites across
the UI (maxHeightGate.ts's MaxHeightGateResult has no `code` field AT ALL despite
citing C58). Those are real and remain OPEN — see ISSUE-LOG.

⚠ THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING IS NOT IN THIS LIST. check-motion-gate-coverage was never on

'R11 structurally retired — no Canvas2D view manager files found at any candidate path'
A FALSE STRUCTURAL CLAIM: apps/editor/src/engine/views holds 83 files. The verdict was
accidentally right and the reasoning entirely fabricated — had PlanViewManager or
SplitViewManager lost beginMotion(), the gate would still have reported 'retired'.
Candidate existence now comes from existsSync, and a candidate that exists but is

test (a match marks a file compliant) running on RAW source, so a file carrying
'// TODO: add beginMotion()' counted as having done it. Comment-stripped now.
Two judgement calls stated rather than buried. check-structuredclone flips verdict on
comment-stripping (188 mentions > ceiling 157; 119 CODE uses < 157) — the assertion is
about calls, and a comment saying 'do not call structuredClone' is not a call, so
stripping is the CORRECT measurement, not a weakening; both numbers print on every run.
check-no-workspacemountbridge deliberately does NOT strip comments: its assertion is that
the class NAME must not reappear anywhere, and the D.4 closure scrubbed 18 comment

2026-08-11 · §LEDGERED-LEVEL (C9) — THE LEDGER NOW RECORDS A LEVEL, NOT JUST A NAME.
Three entries live here, and until today all three said the same single thing — 'this
gate fails' — with no way to distinguish failing AS DECLARED from failing WORSE. Every
reading above every threshold exited 1 and was absorbed identically, so a ledgered gate
silently licensed its own growth. That is R7 one level in, and it was not theoretical:
• check-xss-guards was ALREADY WORSE and nobody could see it. Measured today:
apps/editor/src/ui/import-manager/ImportManagerPanel.ts 7 -> 11 and
apps/editor/src/ui/layout/GISAreaLayout.ts 16 -> 20 — EIGHT unguarded HTML-sink
interpolations that entered after the freeze and were reported, run after run, under
a yellow KNOWN-DEBT line. Its per-file-ratchet branch and its zero-tolerance branch
now exit 3, which no ledger absorbs. THE ENTRY STAYS (the baselined debt is still
tolerated) but it can no longer cover growth. The eight are a PRODUCTION blocker in
another stream's files; nothing in tools/ga-gate can fix them.
• check-no-commandmanager now carries LEDGERED_LITERAL/WINDOW/CM_EXEC = 11/62/62,
measured today (the note above recorded literal=14; the honest reading has FALLEN to
11, so the declared level falls with it). At or under: exit 1, absorbable. Above any
one of them: exit 3.
• check-custom-event-apps now carries LEDGERED_LEVEL = 20 (was recorded 26 above;
measured 20 today, so the declared level falls). Ratchet baseline unchanged at 4.
None of these is a new threshold to spend. A LEDGERED_ constant is a record of how bad
the debt was when someone last looked, and it may only ever fall — raising one converts
a measurement into a permission, which is the failure the ratchet exists to prevent.
2026-08-12 · §NEWLY-MEASURED — THERE IS NOW A THIRD STATE, AND IT IS NOT IN THIS FILE.
The two states declared at the top of this comment are exhaustive only for gates that
existed before the reading. BIM 3.0 Phase 1 produces a gate that is BUILT THIS WEEK and
lands RED on defects that PREDATE it. Rule 1 would call that a REGRESSION, which says the
tree got worse on the day someone wrote a scanner. Rule 3 would make it DECLARED DEBT,
which backdates a decision nobody made — nobody CHOSE to ship these; nothing was measuring
them. Both labels are wrong, in opposite directions.
Those gates go in the SIBLING FILE `tools/ga-gate/gate-newly-measured.json`, whose
$comment carries the full argument for why it is a separate file and not a section here.
The short version: rule 3 attaches a founder decision to CHOOSING TO SHIP A VIOLATION, and
that rule must not leak onto CHOOSING TO START MEASURING — putting an approval step in
front of turning an instrument on is how instruments do not get built
(BIM30-READINESS-GATES §2.3).
RULES 1-3 ABOVE ARE UNCHANGED. What changed is that rule 1's 'NOT on this list' now means
'on NEITHER list'. The one join between the files is deliberate and narrow: MOVING an entry
from gate-newly-measured.json INTO this file — i.e. deciding to live with a defect that was
merely unmeasured before — IS a rule-3 addition and needs the founder. So does extending a
reviewBy date over there. Nothing may be in both files; run-all refuses that outright.
Residency and discovery for the two gate HOMES (tools/ga-gate/ vs
tools/rac-conformance/certification/gates/) are settled by BIM30-READINESS-GATES §2.1 as
amended the same day. Both homes import the ONE exit-code implementation at
tools/rac-conformance/certification/contract.ts; neither copies it.
